properties.label: Staten Island Ferry round trip (free, about 25 min each way)

properties.name: Whitehall Terminal & the Staten Island Ferry
properties.story: Sofia's commute. In the first episode she pre-games on the ferry into Manhattan, then picks a fight with three trolls outside Sean's, a dingy Irish bar near this terminal, and sleeps it off in a pile of trash bags. Later she rides the ferry with Jackson, who explains the Order of the Concrete Fist and its prophecy of a chosen one as the boat passes the Statue of Liberty (Eps. 7 and 11).
properties.visit: The ferry is free and runs around the clock. The crossing takes about 25 minutes each way and passes close to the Statue of Liberty. At St. George you have to get off and walk round to board the next boat back. Sofia's Staten Island (her house, the bakery, the Monastery of the Midnight Sun) is never located in the show, so the ride itself is the stop.

properties.name: Wall Street & the New York Stock Exchange
properties.story: Robert Moses' home turf. Ricky's spell to find the stolen Key to the City goes blank in a magical dead zone among the Wall Street towers (Ep. 7). In the Showdown at the Stock Exchange the party bursts onto the trading floor, where Moses forges Sinatra's Law and opens the Golden Door. Pete is killed and revived, and Ricky beheads Moses (Eps. 13 and 14). Pete later sneaks into Moses' hedge-fund office nearby (Ep. 15).
properties.visit: There are no public visits inside the exchange. The columned front on Broad St is the classic view, with the Fearless Girl statue facing it. Trinity Church, at the head of Wall St, marks one edge of the episode's dead zone.

properties.name: City Hall
properties.story: Past a magical security checkpoint staffed by a goblin clerk, Kingston gives his testimony about the attack on Santa and argues with Liz (Ep. 7). Kingston's wedding photo, which Pete notices in his apartment, was taken at City Hall (Ep. 3).
properties.visit: City Hall Park is open to everyone. The building itself can only be seen on scheduled tours.

properties.name: Tompkins Square Park
properties.story: Esther brings holiday gifts to her blind witch mother and grandmother in a frosty grotto here. They search Ricky's heart for darkness, find none, and give Esther a prophecy (Ep. 11). On New Year's Eve Kugrash uses the Rat Crown to break the curse on Esther's family, freeing the three witches, and the park's trees swallow the Maserati (Ep. 15).
properties.visit: The walk here from Astor Place runs along St. Marks Place. The park is busiest around its central paths and dog runs.

properties.name: Union Square
properties.story: After the journey through Nod, Wally's L train delivers the party back to the waking world at 14 St-Union Sq. Pete hugs Kingston, Ricky downs a 1000-hour energy drink, and Sofia finally tells everyone that Dale is dead. Misty suggests pizza on University Place (Ep. 9).
properties.visit: The station below is one of the city's busiest hubs (4 5 6, L, N Q R W). The park hosts a greenmarket several days a week.

properties.name: Empire State Building
properties.story: The 'pinnacle' at the end of Dale's chosen-one quest. On New Year's Eve Sofia climbs the outside of the building, past the closed observation deck, to the very top of the spire, and chooses herself as the Concrete Fist's chosen one (Ep. 15).
properties.visit: The observation decks on the 86th and 102nd floors are ticketed. For a free view of the spire, look up from 5th Ave at 33rd St.

properties.name: New York Public Library (Stephen A. Schwarzman Building)
properties.story: A secret door by the stone lions leads to the upside-down halls of the Gramercy Occult Society. The party first assembles on these steps (Ep. 1), brings back the twins sick with peppermint disease (Ep. 3) and holds a tense secret meeting about Pete (Ep. 7). On New Year's Eve the steps are strewn with bodies, a lion is cracked, and the Umbral Engine below has been sabotaged (Ep. 15).
properties.visit: Free to enter during opening hours. Don't miss the Rose Main Reading Room on the third floor. The show calls the lions Orlando and Rovias; their real names are Patience and Fortitude.

properties.name: Grand Central Terminal
properties.story: Home of the clock gnomes. Shrunk to matchbox size, the party tumbles through the food court, where Pete lands on an oyster and Kugrash rescues him as a giant eagle (Ep. 11). On New Year's Eve Rowan holds a fae war council at the Whispering Gallery and the clock, then rides a dragon train from a secret yard toward Times Square (Ep. 15).
properties.visit: Try the Whispering Gallery outside the Oyster Bar on the lower level: stand in opposite corners of the arches and whisper into the wall. The four-faced clock sits on the information booth in the main concourse.

properties.name: Times Square & the Theater District
properties.story: The story begins and ends here. The party's first fight is against a hive of mutant Santa clones around a giant ice chrysalis (Eps. 1 and 2). A few blocks away, Misty's opening night of 'Midsummer Nights' becomes the Broadway Brawl against Titania (Eps. 11 and 12; the theater is never named). At midnight on New Year's Eve the Golden Door opens over the ball drop. In the battle inside Robert Moses' phylactery storm, Kugrash eats the Bagel of All Things and scatters into the city (Eps. 15 to 17).
properties.visit: Come after dark. The theaters are on the side streets between W 44th and W 47th St, and any of them can stand in for Misty's.

properties.description: 6 train Brooklyn Bridge-City Hall to Astor Pl

properties.name: Central Park South
properties.story: Misty Moore's glass-walled penthouse overlooks the park from one of these buildings; it's the most-visited place in Chapter 1. Kugrash and Sofia crawl in through a boiler vent (Ep. 1), Titania's cursed mirror breaks Misty's hip (Ep. 5), and Robert Moses offers her a way out of the fae court at her holiday party (Ep. 11). Once Misty is reborn as Rowan Berry, Rowan inherits the place (Ep. 13).
properties.visit: The building is fictional and unnamed. Walk in at the 6th Ave gate and follow the paths north to the Mall.

properties.name: Bethesda Terrace & Fountain
properties.story: The Angel of the Waters on top of the fountain is Em, who gives Sofia and Kugrash healing water (Ep. 3). When the statue is stolen, the party follows its celestial drag marks down a manhole to rescue her (Eps. 3 and 4). At the Loeb Boathouse next door, Kugrash breaks into a locker for a pair of loafers, which Sofia turns down (Ep. 3).
properties.visit: The angel is real: Emma Stebbins' statue, unveiled in 1873. Walk down under the terrace to see the tiled arcade.

properties.name: The Ramble & Belvedere Castle
properties.story: Santa's sleigh crashes in a clearing near Belvedere Castle. Kugrash and Sofia find the reindeer cut loose, peppermint blood and faerie ivy from Nod (Eps. 1 and 2). In the Ramble, a birch-tree arch opens onto the Faerie Glen, where the party crashes the wedding of Don Confetti's daughter with pigeon plus-ones (Eps. 3 and 5).
properties.visit: The Ramble's paths twist on purpose, so leave time to get a little lost. Belvedere Castle overlooks Turtle Pond and is free to visit.

properties.name: The Met: Temple of Dendur
properties.story: Robert Moses summons Kingston to the Temple of Dendur, where Kingston once fought a mummy, and threatens his friends. Kingston slaps him, leaving an ash handprint (Ep. 13).
properties.visit: Admission is ticketed. The temple stands in its own glass-walled gallery, the Sackler Wing, on the first floor. If you skip the museum, the steps on 5th Ave are a fine stop.

properties.name: The Reservoir
properties.story: Under the water lies the ancient cistern where the old aqueduct enters the city: the Rat King's lair. He means to marry the stolen angel statue. The party fights him in a flooding chamber, and Kugrash takes his crown (Eps. 3 and 4). In the first episode Kugrash scurries through the subway tunnels under the park, reached by a manhole on one of the transverse roads.
properties.visit: A 1.58-mile running track circles the Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis Reservoir. The skyline view south across the water is the one on the postcards.

properties.name: Harlem: 125th Street
properties.story: Kingston's neighborhood. The Brown family's three-story house, St. Owen's Hospital (where Kingston works as a nurse) and Cosmo's corner store are all 'right off 125th Street'. The house becomes the party's headquarters, and the Browns host Pete for Christmas (Ep. 11). In the epilogue Pete works at a second-hand bookstore around the corner (Ep. 17).
properties.visit: None of these places is a real address. The Apollo Theater (253 W 125th St) is a few blocks west, on the way to the next train.

properties.name: Clinton Hill: the Chantry
properties.story: The Gramercy Occult Society's Brooklyn branch is an ivy-covered brownstone with a gargoyle door knocker named Frank. Esther briefs Ricky on the SantaCon clones here (Ep. 1), the party learns that the 'gray baby' is Nod, monarch of the Sixth Borough (Ep. 5), and Don Confetti confesses inside a runic circle (Ep. 13).
properties.visit: The Chantry is fictional, but the brownstones and mansions along Clinton Avenue fit the description. Pratt Institute's campus is a few blocks away.

properties.name: Lorimer St station (L)
properties.story: Pete teleports onto the Canarsie-bound platform with the dying Nod, and everyone converges for the Subway Skirmish. Kugrash's rats kill the crooked cop Epona and eat her onyx badge, and Pizza Rat's die summons the L train to Nod. It runs on the wrong side of the track, out of Brooklyn and into the Sixth Borough (Eps. 7 and 8).
properties.visit: End the day like the party: board a Canarsie-bound L here. In the waking world it stops at Canarsie-Rockaway Pkwy. Union Pool, mentioned at the table, is across the street.

properties.description: C train 125 St to Clinton-Washington Avs
G train Clinton-Washington Avs to Metropolitan Av

properties.name: Green-Wood Cemetery
properties.story: Sofia mourns at Dale Lee's grave, where Jackson tells her Dale was a monk of the Concrete Fist who was meant to be the chosen one (Ep. 11).
properties.visit: Free to visit. Enter at the Gothic main gate at 5th Ave and 25th St.

properties.name: Steinway Street, Astoria
properties.story: The dream-insect invasion: Astoria's storefronts are webbed over by gentrifying bugs. Sofia frees La Gran Gata from her 'bodega of wonders' and becomes her chosen (Eps. 5 to 7).
properties.visit: The party bursts out of the Steinway St subway entrance. The bodega is fictional.

properties.name: Cobble Hill
properties.story: Ricky's introduction: he carries a girl out of a burning railroad-apartment building, secretly casts Create Water, and gives an interview to NY1 (Ep. 1).
properties.visit: The building is never named. Cobble Hill Park is a pleasant center for a stroll among the brownstones.

properties.name: Bushwick
properties.story: Priya's art show in a condemned loft 'in the heart of Bushwick' goes up in flames. Kugrash, as a tiny King Kong, topples the water tower, and Sofia kills Isabella (Eps. 9 and 10).
properties.visit: The loft is fictional. The Bushwick Collective's street murals around Troutman St and St Nicholas Ave match the art-scene mood.

properties.name: Greenpoint waterfront
properties.story: Pete's story opens with a checkup at Dr. Lugash's unlicensed clinic in a warehouse by the water. A reflection in a ceiling puddle tells him magic is real (Ep. 1).
properties.visit: The warehouse is fictional. WNYC Transmitter Park, at the end of Greenpoint Ave, looks across the river at Midtown.

properties.name: Williamsburg waterfront
properties.story: Kingston walks over from Clinton Hill to meet Willy the golem near Kent Ave. Willy buys him a bagel and Kingston drives out a nest of dybbuks (Ep. 5).
properties.visit: Domino Park, on Kent Ave, is the place to see the waterfront.

properties.name: Queensboro Bridge
properties.story: Ricky sprints across the 59th Street Bridge with his ox, Ox, chasing the stolen Key to the City, and #MarchInDecember goes viral (Ep. 7).
properties.visit: The bridge has a path for people on foot and bikes, so you can follow Ricky's sprint.

properties.name: Yankee Stadium
properties.story: On New Year's Eve the Hall of Heroes appears at the stadium. After a game of catch, Ricky's Questing Blade receives its secret blessing (Ep. 15).
properties.visit: Right outside 161 St-Yankee Stadium station.

properties.name: Forest Hills
properties.story: Kugrash's son David lives here. Kugrash, as a dog, spends Christmas with his grandkids (Ep. 11).
properties.visit: The house is fictional. Station Square in Forest Hills Gardens is the neighborhood's showpiece.

properties.name: Battery Park & Castle Clinton
properties.story: When the party decides to strike at Ellis Island, a ferry is waiting for Kingston, the Vox Populi, piloted by his bus driver turned captain (Ep. 14). Next door at Whitehall Terminal, the group meets to take the Staten Island Ferry to the monastery; Pete makes it just as the boat departs (Ep. 6).
properties.visit: Ferry tickets for the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island are sold at Castle Clinton and online. There is airport-style security before boarding, so arrive early. The free Staten Island Ferry leaves from Whitehall Terminal, a few minutes' walk east.

properties.name: Ellis Island
properties.story: The chapter's big set piece. In the story the museum is closed, chained and being sold to Gladiator. Null strips the heroes of parts of themselves, and they dive into historic photographs in the Great Hall to win them back (Ep. 14). Null erases Iga from time, and a drawing of Holly Branch, with a fragment of the Fairyland sign, opens the way to Faerie (Ep. 15).
properties.visit: The National Museum of Immigration fills the main building, and the Great Hall is on the second floor. Boats from Battery Park stop at Liberty Island first. Allow at least three hours for the round trip.

properties.name: 9/11 Memorial & Museum
properties.story: In Nod, the party finds a Latin inscription on a marble civic building: 'Nulla dies umquam memori vos eximet aevo.' From it, Pete's True Sight wins the enemy's name: Null (Ep. 10). In the waking world, the English version of that line from Virgil's Aeneid ('No day shall erase you from the memory of time') is inscribed in the 9/11 Memorial Museum.
properties.visit: The memorial pools are free and open to all. The museum, where the quotation hangs in Memorial Hall, is ticketed. Please be respectful: this is a memorial.

properties.name: City Hall & the old City Hall station
properties.story: Where Kingston's story starts. In a 1994 flashback, young Kingston takes a call at a payphone on Lafayette St, wanders into the abandoned City Hall station, and finds the dying Dragon of Bleecker Street in a treasure-lined burrow. The dragon makes him the Vox Populi, gives him a subway token, and vanishes as a 4 train pulls into Brooklyn Bridge-City Hall (Ep. 1). Years later Kingston goes back to the same payphone to call for help (Ep. 13). The courthouses on Foley Square, just north, are the marble Civic Center that Nod mirrors in Episode 10.
properties.visit: The old City Hall station closed in 1945, but you can still glimpse it: stay aboard a downtown 6 after its last stop at Brooklyn Bridge-City Hall, and the train loops through the old station before heading back uptown.

properties.name: Chinatown: Mott Street
properties.story: The Shen family, draconic sorcerers, live behind a Mott Street door that opens onto an extra-dimensional mountain bridge. They brought the Dragon of Bleecker Street's egg to New York in the 1870s, and they give the party medicines and lore for raising a dragon (Ep. 13). Later Cody rides his moped around Chinatown and Bleecker St hunting for the hidden hoard (Ep. 15).
properties.visit: The party walks in past Columbus Park, where mornings are busy with tai chi and card games. A good place for lunch.

properties.name: The Holland Tunnel & the Hudson
properties.story: Looking across the Hudson, Ricky and Cody see storm clouds massing over New Jersey: the Jersey Devil and his Shore buddies are coming through the tunnel (Ep. 4). The party meets at the Manhattan mouth of the tunnel, where the Questing Blade chooses Cody and becomes a greatsword (Ep. 5), before the fight under the river.
properties.visit: The walk here along Canal and Broome Sts passes the tunnel's entrance plaza. The squat building out on the water at Pier 34 is one of the tunnel's ventilation towers. The tunnel itself is closed to people on foot.

properties.name: West 4th St station & Bleecker Street
properties.story: The 'confluence' of anti-social magic that the demon Bazathrax warns about. The new party assembles on this platform for the first time; a haunted express train skips the stop, and they all leap aboard (Ep. 2). It becomes a runaway northbound A train full of graves, which Ricky stops near the end of the line, at Dyckman St (Ep. 3). Bleecker Street, which gave the dragon its name, crosses 6th Ave just south of here.
properties.visit: It's a two-level station: the A, C and E on one level, the B, D, F and M on the other. To follow the runaway train, take an uptown A to Dyckman St, the second-to-last stop (about 35 minutes). Washington Square Park is a block east.

properties.name: Herald Square & the parade route
properties.story: Thanksgiving: the party is watching the Macy's parade from the crowd when true clowns from the Dreaming knock out Wally Claus, cut the lines and fly off on four giant balloons. The fight continues in the air over Midtown (Ep. 7).
properties.visit: The real parade ends here at Macy's on Thanksgiving morning. The story never says where the party stands.

properties.name: Empire State Building
properties.story: In Nod, the top of the Empire State Building is where Pete finds a hole leaking raw Umbra into the Dreaming (Eps. 6 and 7). Iga's family chest carves a picture of Sofia and Ricky on top of the building (Eps. 1 and 4).
properties.visit: The observation decks on the 86th and 102nd floors are ticketed. For a free view of the spire, look up from 5th Ave at 33rd St.

properties.name: New York Public Library (Stephen A. Schwarzman Building)
properties.story: The Gramercy Occult Society, hidden behind the lions, is the chapter's nerve center. Esther's rune map raises the alarm about the Holland Tunnel (Ep. 5), and JJ moves in and builds a time-travel watch (Ep. 14). In 'Treachery at Gramercy' the party fights Tony Simos in the Umbral Engine chamber beneath the library (Ep. 16), where Dale comes back to life (Ep. 17).
properties.visit: Free to enter during opening hours. Don't miss the Rose Main Reading Room on the third floor. The show calls the lions Orlando and Rovias; their real names are Patience and Fortitude.

properties.name: Grand Central Terminal
properties.story: The party whispers into the corners of the Whispering Gallery to summon the clock gnomes. The gnomes shrink everyone into a matchbox and lend them a tiny dragon-headed train that runs on the pipes through the subway to the Bronx (Ep. 11).
properties.visit: The Whispering Gallery is outside the Oyster Bar on the lower level: stand in opposite corners of the arches and whisper into the wall.

properties.name: Upper West Side: W 72nd Street
properties.story: Iga's day job is 'Madam Anastasia', a half-basement psychic shop on W 72nd near Columbus Ave. She reads Sofia's tarot (the Tower, the Three of Wands), and a customer named Yagdash, bringing drug money to launder, shoots himself in the backside (Ep. 1).
properties.visit: The shop is fictional, but the block is full of half-basement storefronts like it. The Dakota stands at the corner of W 72nd St and Central Park West, on the way into the park.

properties.name: Central Park: the Carousel
properties.story: The chapter's last scene: two or three years on, everyone meets for a huge family barbecue in Central Park, by the carousel the new mayor saved (Ep. 18). Earlier, Ricky trains by swinging through the park's trees like monkey bars (Ep. 6).
properties.visit: The carousel sits in the middle of the park at about 65th St.

properties.name: The Met: Arms and Armor
properties.story: Nod's mirror of the Met, the Metropolitan Museum of Memories, hosts the Fight at the Museum. In the Arms and Armor wing the party frees the chained Unicorn of New York from animated suits of armor, and Cody fuses Excalibur with his Thirsting Blade (Ep. 9). Deeper in, the Hall of Memories reveals the erasing entity that took earlier Voxes Phantasma (Ep. 10).
properties.visit: Admission is ticketed. The Arms and Armor galleries, with their mounted knights, are on the first floor.

properties.name: Central Park North: 110th Street
properties.story: The finale. The Dragon of Bleecker Street's hoard has been moved under this station and hidden by the Umbral Arcana, until Kingston finally recognizes the way down (Eps. 15 and 17). Below, the egg hatches, the party defeats Null, Iga breaks back into time, and the newborn dragon Langston becomes Kingston and Liz's son (Eps. 17 and 18).
properties.visit: The 2 and 3 trains stop at the corner of 110th St and Malcolm X Blvd. The walk here from the Met passes the Conservatory Garden and the Harlem Meer.

properties.name: Harlem: 125th Street
properties.story: Kingston's block, now under threat. He lives in the family building with Liz, and St. Owen's, Cosmo's corner store and Pete's job at the Uncommon Knowledge bookstore are all just off 125th St. Reggie's electronics shop suddenly stands empty, and Excelsior Dynamic Homes is buying up the neighborhood (Eps. 1 and 4). The Browns host Thanksgiving for the party (Ep. 8).
properties.visit: None of these places is a real address. The Apollo Theater is a few blocks west on 125th.

properties.description: S train Grand Central-42 St to Times Sq-42 St
1 train Times Sq-42 St to 72 St

properties.name: Astoria
properties.story: Pete and Cody's house share, the most-visited place in Chapter 2, is somewhere in Astoria, more than 20 minutes' walk from the subway. On Steinway St, Bazathrax bursts out of a smoking manhole (Ep. 2), and at the Neptune Diner, Maddie Park joins the fight against Gladiator (Ep. 14).
properties.visit: The house is fictional and unlocated. Steinway St is a lively shopping street; start at the Steinway St station.

properties.name: Greenpoint: Manhattan Avenue
properties.story: The Lisowski family home, where Iga keeps the ancient carved chest that holds a castle, and where her family cooks a huge Polish Thanksgiving in the castle's ovens (Ep. 8).
properties.visit: The home is fictional. Manhattan Avenue is the heart of Greenpoint's Polish community, full of bakeries and delis.

properties.name: Clinton Hill
properties.story: Ricky and Esther now live above the Chantry, in a tall building with a miniature clock tower on top. The party plans its expedition into Nod at their loft (Eps. 8 and 9).
properties.visit: Fictional. The brownstones along Clinton Avenue fit the neighborhood.

properties.name: Manhattan Bridge walkway
properties.story: Sofia, newly a Shadow monk, hops across the rooftops from the Brooklyn end of the Manhattan Bridge toward Clinton Hill, breaking up a toxic couple on the way (Ep. 2).
properties.visit: The bridge's walkway starts at Jay and Sands Sts in Brooklyn and has big views of the Brooklyn Bridge.

properties.name: Queens Center Mall (Fairyland)
properties.story: Cody sells his soul in his old Hot Topic inside the shuttered mall to save it from Gladiator (Ep. 1). Gladiator builds its time-compression machine here, and in the epilogue Rowan's Fairyland reopens on part of the site (Ep. 18).
properties.visit: A real, open shopping mall. It stands on the site of Fairyland, a real kiddie amusement park from the mid-20th century.

properties.name: Green-Wood Cemetery
properties.story: At Dale's grave, Dale gives back the Questing Blade, disguised as nunchucks, and tells Sofia he'll stop visiting so she can live her life (Ep. 4).
properties.visit: Free to visit. Enter at the Gothic main gate at 5th Ave and 25th St.

properties.name: Dyckman St station (A)
properties.story: Where the runaway A train finally stops, the 'second to last station' on the line. Pete sees raw Umbral Arcana ebbing like a tide on the platform (Ep. 3).
properties.visit: Fort Tryon Park and the Cloisters are a short walk south and uphill.
